popularity.caveat: Counts Qt development-package installations, not QJsonDocument or JSON use; cannot be ranked directly against JSON-specific package counts.

blocker: Compiling qjsonparser.cpp beside QtCore does not make QJsonDocument::fromJson use the local instrumented parser. Compiling local qjsondocument.cpp plus qjsonparser.cpp against the pinned distribution QtCore fails because private parser dependencies are not exported. Adding the matching qcborvalue.cpp and qstringconverter.cpp sources still leaves unresolved qt_to_latin1_unchecked, qt_cbor_stream_set_error, qt_cbor_append_string_chunk, and QLatin1::convertToUnicode symbols from further QtCore implementation files. No linked parser-only target or feedback receipt was obtained. A dedicated pinned source build of QtCore is required before selecting this path.
scope: Only build/link attempts; no malformed-input tests or fuzzing campaign.

metric_decision.rule: PROTOCOL.md Popularity: a primary-unranked C/C++ path whose multi-library source makes the count format-ambiguous may use a format-specific binary development-package installation count of at least 1,000 (at most three such paths per cell).

libqt6core6t64.reason: whole QtCore runtime; no JSON-only binary package exists

metric_decision.result: Metric decision 2026-11-17: Qt cannot qualify regardless of the technical blocker. QJsonDocument lives in QtCore, so the Debian sources qtbase-opensource-src (96,909) and qt6-base (67,857) cover whole multi-library frameworks and their sourcemax counts are format-ambiguous. PROTOCOL.md's fallback then needs a format-specific binary development package with at least 1,000 installations; Qt has none (qt6-base-dev 4,942 is framework-wide and libqt6core6t64 covers all of QtCore). The path was not built further.
